options.content:
# Relations charts from a live Prometheus — **no transformations**

The same eight charts as **ECharts Relations — live Prometheus**, the same
queries against the same `$prom`, with the transformation chain deleted. Seven of the eight
panels below have an **empty Transform tab**.

What does the reshaping instead is a transformation the *plugin* registers on itself
(`longToWide`, via `setDataTransformations`), which runs upstream of the Transform tab:

    SceneQueryRunner → PanelPluginDataTransformer → SceneDataTransformer (user)

It claims exactly one shape — **one series per frame, endpoints in `field.labels`** — which
is what `Format: Time series` returns from any labelled datasource, and pivots it into one
frame with one field per edge. Needs Grafana 13.2+ with
`grafana.panelPluginTransformations`.

**Without the flag every panel here still draws its full topology** — the reader collects
every frame that looks like edges, so N series are N edges. What it loses is **identity**:
each frame's value field is called `Value`, so every edge shares one `field.name`, a
`byName` override matches all of them at once and the override picker lists `Value` once per
frame. The pivot is what turns a model id into a real field, and only a transformation
running before `applyFieldOverrides` can do that. Turn the flag off and compare the override
picker — that is the difference this dashboard is really demonstrating.

### What that deletes, and what it does not

| the instant route | here |
| --- | --- |
| `Format: Table` + `Type: Instant` | `Format: Time series` + `Type: Range` |
| `label_join(…, "id", "-->", …)` | gone — the id comes from the labels |
| the literal `-->` in PromQL | gone |
| `organize` + `rowsToFields` | gone |
| `src`/`dst` to dodge the legacy pre-pass | gone — a labelled series is not the row format |
| two `label_replace`s | gone on the service-graph panels — `client`/`server` is read directly |

`label_replace` is nearly gone too. The reader accepts a short list of **conventional
endpoint pairs** now — `source`/`target`, `client`/`server`, `src`/`dst`, `from`/`to` — so the
service-graph panels (1, 3, 4, 5, 8) are the aggregation and nothing else:

```promql
topk($topk,
  sum by (client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total[$__range]))
)
```

The pair a query grouped by is recorded on the pivoted frame
(`meta.custom.relationsEndpointLabels`), which is what makes the ad-hoc filters below work
with nothing configured. Panels **2**, **6** and **7** keep the rename, because
`cluster`/`namespace` and `server_k8s_*` are not conventions the reader can guess — that is
the remaining case, and the one the Advanced option exists for.

### The row dimension is the payoff

An instant query is one row per edge, so `Reduce` was a decoration — every reducer returned
the same number. A range query is a real row dimension the pivot keeps, so `calcs[0]` is a
choice: panels 1, 4 and 8 use `lastNotNull` ("now"), 2, 3, 6 and 7 use `mean` (the window
average) and 5 uses `max` (the peak).

### Two things measured against this datasource

- **`topk` inside a range query runs per step**, so the response can carry far more series
  than `$topk`: `topk(6, …[$__rate_interval])` returned **20** series here, each with holes
  where it left the top set. The rate window is therefore `$__range`, which returned **7** —
  bounded, and the same topology the sibling dashboard draws.
- **Series have different lengths** — 1, 2, 4, 13, 33 and 57 rows over the same hour. They
  are outer-joined on the union of their timestamps, with `null` in the gaps.

### Ids

The pivot takes an edge id from a rendered legend format (`config.displayNameFromDS`), else
the frame name, else `source-->target`. A plain range query here sets **neither** of the
first two — verified — so edges are `client-->server` with nothing configured. Panel 8 sets
a legend format instead, which wins; the endpoints still come from the labels either way.

### Where the work stops: nodes

A node-stat query is long as well, but one endpoint label is not a pair, so the pivot
declines it and nodes come from the edges' endpoints — position, not statistics. **Panel 4**
keeps `organize` + `rowsToFields` for its node query alone, filtered `byRefId`, and is the
honest picture of the gap. Its edges half still needs nothing.

### The variables

All of them are multi-select with `All` = `.*`, so every matcher in every query is `=~`,
never `=`. Prometheus interpolates a multi variable as a regex group — `(a|b)` — even
when one option is selected, which is exactly why `=` would silently match nothing.

| variable | source | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$prom` | datasource picker, `prometheus` | committed pointing at `ops-cortex-dev` |
| `$cluster` | `label_values(traces_service_graph_request_total, client_k8s_cluster_name)` | |
| `$namespace` | `label_values(…{client_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster"}, client_k8s_namespace_name)` | chained on `$cluster` |
| `$client` | `label_values(…{cluster, namespace}, client)` | chained on both |
| `$server` | `label_values(…{cluster, namespace}, server)` | chained on both |
| `$connection` | `label_values(…, connection_type)` | `database`, `messaging_system`, `virtual_node` |
| `$topk` | custom | edge budget per panel |

The service graph carries cluster and namespace **twice**, once per end
(`client_k8s_*` and `server_k8s_*`), so which end a panel filters on is a real choice:

- the dependency maps (1, 4, 8) scope the **client** side — "traffic originating in this
  selection, wherever it goes";
- the chords (3, 7) scope **both** ends, which is what keeps the matrix square;
- the cluster → namespace → service sankey (6) scopes the **server** side, since that is
  the hierarchy it draws.

`$client`/`$server` do not apply to the Kafka graph, where both ends are already pinned.

One consequence worth knowing: the service-graph processor emits **virtual nodes** for
external dependencies — `kafka`, `mysql` and friends come back with
`connection_type="virtual_node"` and **no** `server_k8s_*` labels at all. So any panel
scoped on the server side (6) excludes them by construction, and selecting one as
`$server` empties that panel while the client-scoped panels still draw it. That is the
data being honest, not a broken panel.

### Ad hoc filters

Pin a tooltip (click a node or a link) and the footer offers **Filter on this value** and **Filter out this value**, plus a **Filter for …** button per non-endpoint label. They write into the `$filters` ad-hoc variable above, which Prometheus injects into every query's metric selector.

A **link** puts both its endpoints in the grouped pair, so "Filter on this value" narrows the dashboard to exactly that edge. A **node** cannot: ad-hoc filters are ANDed, and `client="x" AND server="x"` is self-loops, so its positive asserts the source end alone while its negative excludes *both* — "everything that does not touch this node".

That injection is why the key matters. A frame labelled `source`/`target` filters on nothing: `traces_service_graph_request_total` has no such label, so `source="web-api"` reaches the selector and matches zero series.

The service-graph panels need no configuration for this any more — they group by `client`/`server`, the reader recognises the pair, and the filters are written under it. Only **panel 7** still sets **Source/target filter label** (Advanced), because its query renames `client_k8s_cluster_name`/`server_k8s_cluster_name` and then aggregates the originals away, so no response can recover them.

Panels 2 and 6 leave it unset, and that is the honest answer rather than an omission: both are `or`-joined multi-level flows whose two halves relabel from *different* sources (`cluster`→`namespace`, then `namespace`→`workload`), so no single label is "the source" for the panel. Their tooltips fall back to the frame's own keys.

panels.title: Service dependency map — graph
panels.description: Top-$topk service-to-service edges from Tempo's service graph, as a plain ranged query with an empty Transform tab. Each edge is one series; the plugin's registered pivot makes it one field. Scoped on the client side by $cluster / $namespace / $client / $server.

panels.title: CPU requests: cluster → namespace → workload — sankey
panels.description: kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu"} by (cluster, namespace), `or`-joined to namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel for the namespace → workload level, each level relabelled to source/target. No transformations. Reduce: mean over the window, which the instant route could not express.

panels.title: Service call matrix inside $namespace — chord
panels.description: The service graph with $namespace constrained on both ends, which is what makes it a square matrix. No transformations. Reduce: mean.

panels.title: Where the pivot stops: node stats — graph
panels.description:
The same edges as panel 1 with no transformations, plus a node-stat query that still needs the instant + organize + rowsToFields chain: the pivot claims edges only, because one endpoint label is not a pair. The node chain is filtered byRefId so it cannot touch the edges frames. Nodes are coloured by error ratio; the `-->` override puts the edges back on req/s.

The edges half draws either way — the reader collects every frame that looks like edges, pivoted or raw. What the pivot adds is a `field.name` per edge, which is what the `-->` override matches on; with the flag off every edge is called `Value` and that one override paints all of them.

options.content:
### 5 · Kafka fan-in / fan-out — graph (below left)

One `or`-joined query: everything producing into `kafka`, and everything consuming from it.
`$client`/`$server` do not apply — both ends are pinned. `Reduce: Max`, the peak rate in
the window.

```promql
topk($topk,
  sum by (client, server) (
    rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{server="kafka", client_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",
      client_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", client!=""}[$__range])
  )
)
  or
topk($topk,
  sum by (client, server) (
    rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client="kafka", server_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",
      server_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", server!=""}[$__range])
  )
)
```

### 6 · Traffic by cluster → namespace → service — sankey (below right)

Three levels off one metric's server-side label set, `or`-joined. `Reduce: Mean`.

```promql
      topk($topk,
        sum by (server_k8s_cluster_name, server_k8s_namespace_name) (
          rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{server_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", server_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", server=~"$server", server_k8s_cluster_name!="", server_k8s_namespace_name!="", server!=""}[$__range])
        )
      ),
      "source", "$1", "server_k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)"
    ),
    "target", "$1", "server_k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"
  )
)
  or
sum by (source, target) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      topk($topk,
        sum by (server_k8s_namespace_name, server) (
          rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{server_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", server_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", server=~"$server", server_k8s_cluster_name!="", server_k8s_namespace_name!="", server!=""}[$__range])
        )
      ),
      "source", "$1", "server_k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"
    ),
    "target", "$1", "server", "(.*)"
  )
)
```

Server-side k8s labels exclude virtual nodes by construction, so picking an external
dependency as `$server` empties this panel — the data being honest, not a broken panel.

### 7 · Cross-cluster traffic matrix — chord

`Reduce: Mean`.

```promql
sum by (source, target) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      topk($topk,
        sum by (client_k8s_cluster_name, server_k8s_cluster_name) (
          rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", server_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", client_k8s_cluster_name!="", server_k8s_cluster_name!=""}[$__range])
        )
      ),
      "source", "$1", "client_k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)"
    ),
    "target", "$1", "server_k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)"
  )
)
```

### 8 · Parallel edges by `connection_type` — graph

The third label goes in the grouping, so one pair yields several series. `Reduce: Last *`.

```promql
sum by (source, target, connection_type) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      topk($topk,
        sum by (client, server, connection_type) (
          rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client_k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster", client_k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace", client=~"$client", server=~"$server", client!="", server!="", connection_type=~"$connection",
            connection_type!=""}[$__range])
        )
      )
```
`Legend: {{source}} → {{target}} ({{connection_type}})`

The legend format is the id here, which is why these edges are not called
`client-->server`. Without one the pivot still keeps them apart — it appends the label set
that distinguishes them, to *every* member of the clash, giving
`a-->b {connection_type="database"}` and `a-->b {connection_type="messaging_system"}`.
An explicit legend format is simply nicer to read and nicer to write an override against:
the `byRegexp /virtual_node/` below dashes every virtual-node edge.

panels.title: Kafka fan-in / fan-out — graph
panels.description: One `or`-joined query: {server="kafka"} is everything producing into Kafka, {client="kafka"} everything consuming from it. No transformations. Reduce: max — the peak rate in the window, which needs the row dimension the pivot keeps.

panels.title: Traffic by cluster → namespace → service — sankey
panels.description: Three levels from one metric's server-side label set, `or`-joined and relabelled level by level. No transformations. A sankey needs a DAG, so the three levels must not share a name. Requires the server-side k8s labels, so virtual nodes are excluded by construction.

panels.title: Cross-cluster traffic matrix — chord
panels.description: client_k8s_cluster_name → server_k8s_cluster_name, both scoped by $cluster and both required non-empty: a series missing one would relabel to an empty endpoint, which the reader rejects. No transformations. Reduce: mean.

panels.title: Parallel edges by connection_type — graph
panels.description: sum by (source, target, connection_type) gives several series per node pair, filtered by $connection. No transformations. The legend format supplies the id; without one the pivot appends the distinguishing label set to every member of the clash instead.
